as_written_in_papers.quote: A novel heterozygote c.1906+2T>G in TNFAIP3 was detected by gene testing.
| c.1906+2T>G | 15 years | Splice site | Oral and genital ulcers, folliculitis, proteinuria | Positive | A20 haploinsufficiency | [32] |

cases.statement: Two carriers in one family (PMID 35958611, Family 2): the proband P2 (III:5), a 35-year-old woman with oral and genital ulcers from age 15, folliculitis and nephrotic-range proteinuria; and her 13-year-old daughter IV:1 with recurrent fever, oral and genital ulcers and abdominal pain from age 9. Both heterozygous. The review 39125844 (Table 2 row 2) summarises the proband, citing PMID 35958611 as [32].

people.label: P2
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent oral and genital ulcers from age 15; folliculitis; proteinuria from age 32 diagnosed as nephrotic syndrome; moderate anaemia; low-titre ANA

quotes.quote: The proband (III:5, Figure 1D) of the second family (P2) was a 35-year-old Chinese Han woman who had suffered from recurrent oral and genital ulcers since age 15.
She also had folliculitis in recent years, without recurrent fever, polyarthritis, or uveitis.
Regarding her medical history, she developed proteinuria at age 32 and was diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome.
CBC showed moderate anemia with a hemoglobin level of 89 g/L.
Serum autoantibodies were all negative except for a low-titer ANA (1:80).

people.label: IV:1 (Family 2)
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent fever, oral ulcers, genital ulcers and abdominal pain from age 9, monthly 3-4-day episodes

quotes.quote: Pedigree analysis (Figure 1D) revealed that her 13-year-old daughter (IV:1) had suffered from recurrent fever, oral ulcers, genital ulcers and abdominal pain since the age of nine.
Each episode lasted 3 to 4 days monthly.
Gene testing demonstrated the TNFAIP3 c.1906+2T>G heterozygous variant in the proband’s daughter.

people.label: Table 2 row 2
people.key_phenotypes: review summary of the proband: oral and genital ulcers, folliculitis, proteinuria

quotes.quote: | c.1906+2T>G | 15 years | Splice site | Oral and genital ulcers, folliculitis, proteinuria | Positive | A20 haploinsufficiency | [32] |
The proband patient experienced folliculitis and oral and genital ulcers since her teenage years, without fever, polyarthritis, or uveitis.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Both carriers have recurrent oral and genital ulcers, a Behçet-like pattern the authors treat as typical of HA20. Testing was by whole-exome sequencing; the text names no other candidate variant for Family 2 and does not state which other causes were excluded (TB-SPOT negative in the proband).

quotes.quote: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) by next-generation sequencing was performed in the Center for Genetic Testing, Joy Orient Translational Medicine Research Centre Co., Ltd., Beijing, China.
TB-SPOT was negative.
We suggest that HA20 should be considered in child-onset patients with manifestations that resemble BS, especially those whose family members have similar symptoms.

segregation.statement: One affected relative carries the variant: the proband's daughter (IV:1). Three further relatives with recurrent oral ulcers (aunt II:3, cousins III:3 and III:4) were not tested. No unaffected relatives' genotypes are given in the text.

quotes.quote: Gene testing demonstrated the TNFAIP3 c.1906+2T>G heterozygous variant in the proband’s daughter.
One of her aunts (II:3) and two cousins (III:3, III:4) had recurrent oral ulcers but no fever, arthritis, vulva ulcers, follicles, or abdominal pain.
Her aunt and cousins refused to do the gene testing for personal reasons.

functional.statement: Patient material from the proband P2 (blood RNA, PBMCs), compared with healthy controls (n=3 for cytokines). RT-PCR: an extra band 500-1000 bp longer than wild type, read as intron 7 retention, and brighter than the wild-type band. Immunoblot: reduced basal and TNF-α- or LPS-induced A20; more IKK and NF-κB phosphorylation; more NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β. TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β raised in plasma and culture supernatant. The daughter's cells were not tested.

quotes.quote: Agarose gel electrophoresis showed that c.1906+2T>G had an additional band between 2500 bp and 3000 bp (Figure 2C ②), which was approximately 500-1000 bp longer than the wild-type band (Figure 2C ①, 1998 bp), suggesting that this splice site variant resulted in intron 7 retention.
Comparing the brightness of these two bands, we found that the variant c.1906+2T>G was more dominant than WT at the transcriptional level.
At the protein level, immunoblotting of PBMC lysates derived from P2 and healthy controls confirmed reduced basal, TNF-α- or LPS-induced expression of A20 (Figure 2D).
As a consequence of reduced A20 expression, the phosphorylation of IKK and NF-kB, the key components of the NF-κB signaling pathway, was more pronounced in P2-derived PBMCs than in control cells.
We observed exaggerated NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β in P2-derived PBMCs after stimulation by LPS or TNF-α, especially the former.

Resulting from active NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathways, the proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β were all increased both in plasma and cell culture supernatant compared with controls (Figure 2E).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice donor variant (+2); predicted protein p.? per the batch HGVS. The paper reports intron 7 retention and reduced A20 protein, and links reduced A20 to NF-κB and NLRP3 activation.

quotes.quote: Abnormal A20 expression was believed to account for the activation of the NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling pathways as well as high levels of proinflammatory cytokines in the proband of the second family.
Further functional experiments showed that c.1906+2T>G resulted in splice site mutation and reduced A20 expression.

computational_predictions.statement: Alamut predicted an effect on splicing; NetGene2 and BDGP were used to look for splice sites in intron 7. No scores are given.

quotes.quote: For the splice site variant c.1906+2T>G, potential splice sites in intron 7 were analyzed using NetGene2 and BDGP.

Since the minor allele frequency of c.1906+2T>G in the noncoding region is lower than 0.0001 in the Asian population and Alamut functional software predicted that it might affect the splicing of the protein, we think it might play a role in the clinical manifestation of the proband and her daughter of the second family.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Minor allele frequency stated as below 0.0001 in the Asian population (database not named).

quotes.quote: Since the minor allele frequency of c.1906+2T>G in the noncoding region is lower than 0.0001 in the Asian population and Alamut functional software predicted that it might affect the splicing of the protein, we think it might play a role in the clinical manifestation of the proband and her daughter of the second family.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it novel and state it was validated as pathogenic in their study. No ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: Two novel variants, A547T and c.1906+2T>G, were validated to be pathogenic in our study.
Among the three TNFAIP3 variants detected in these HA20 patients, two novel variants, A547T and c.1906+2T>G, had never been validated to be pathogenic.

concerns: The paper contradicts itself on fever: the text says the proband had no recurrent fever and the daughter had recurrent fever, but Table 1 marks fever + for the 35-year-old (onset 15) and – for the daughter (onset 9). The two rows' fever entries look swapped.
The daughter is '13-year-old' in the text but age at diagnosis 12 in Table 1.

Numbering: Table 1 labels the variant '(exon 7)' although it is intronic (+2; the text says intron 7). The paper's transcript is NM_006290 (Table 1 header; NM_006290.4 in the Figure 1 legend for Family 1). The batch uses NM_001270508.2; the panel should confirm the numbering matches.
39125844 (review) is a secondary summary of the proband P2 (HA20-ID0203), not an independent case.
Same splice donor site as G-ha20-052 (c.1906+1G>C, PMID 34030699).
notes_for_panel: Two-generation family: an affected mother and an affected daughter both carry the variant, plus three untested relatives with oral ulcers. RNA and protein studies on the proband's own cells. De novo status is not applicable or not reported.
